event: Single-mode glass optical waveguides with radiation loss about 7 dB/km, near intrinsic scattering; 60-70 dB/km total; bending losses measured; lowest total about 20 dB/km.
event_locator: p.2 abstract and text; p.3; p.4
dri: D. B. Keck; R. D. Maurer; F. P. Kapron
dri_locator: p.2 byline (F. P. Kapron, D. B. Keck, R. D. Maurer; no roles stated)
orgs_printed: Research and Development Laboratories, Corning Glass Works, Corning, New York
key_figure_caption: Radiation, absorption and total loss coefficients (dB/km) versus bend radius of curvature (2-10 cm) for two single-mode waveguides, A and B.
key_figure_reason: measured loss components behind the radiation and bending-loss conclusions
notes: Received 1970-08-07 (p.2). APL vol. 17 no. 10, 15 November 1970, pp.423-425 = text.md pp.2-4; text.md p.1 is a publisher cover sheet and p.2 opens with the end of a preceding dosimetry letter (its Fig. 4). All losses measured with a He-Ne laser at 632.8 nm (p.3). The about 20 dB/km is the lowest total attenuation observed in all waveguides made for the work (p.2); the two 30-m sections studied had 60-70 dB/km total. Intrinsic waveguide scattering 5 +/- 1 dB/km is calculated from bulk-glass scattering; the measured radiation loss is 7 +/- 2 dB/km (p.3). The paper says 'glass' and does not name silica or the core / cladding compositions; core diameter 3-4 um, cladding-core diameter ratio about 60:1 (p.2). No 'first' claim. DRI kept from papers.csv (external evidence): the paper states no roles. Acknowledgment: P. C. Schultz for glass composition work, F. Zimar for waveguide construction help, L. L. Carpenter for technical assistance (p.4). Postal code omitted.
